title: Balanced trios
prompt:
Each reading is a signed sensor offset; return every distinct value triple [a, b, c], taken from three different positions, whose sum is exactly 0.

- readings has 0 to 3,000 integers between -10^5 and 10^5.
- Each triple is listed once, with a <= b <= c, and two triples are the same if they have the same values.
- Sort the triples in ascending lexicographic order (by a, then b, then c). Return [] if there are none.
hints: Trying every triple is O(n^3). Sorting first makes both the search and the duplicate handling easier.
Fix the smallest value a = sorted[i]; you now need a pair in the rest of the sorted list summing to -a, which two pointers find in O(n).
Skip i when sorted[i] equals sorted[i - 1]. After recording a match, move both pointers and skip repeats of the values you just used.

solution.explanation: After sorting, each choice of the smallest value reduces the task to a two-pointer pair search on the suffix. Skipping equal neighbours for i, lo and hi ensures each value triple is emitted once. Because i increases and lo increases within each i, the output is already in lexicographic order.

complexity.notes: Sorting costs O(n log n), dominated by the O(n) pair search for each of n anchors. Space is for the sorted copy (O(1) extra if sorting in place), excluding the output.

followUps: Generalise to triples summing to an arbitrary target, or to quadruples.
Count triples with sum below a target instead of listing those equal to 0.
